the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.bio: Podcast: Jev: The AI That Makes Decisions, Not Text - and Why It Changes Everything (Diogo Almeida)

html_en:
The AI industry is grappling with two defining tensions at once: how to make models more reliable and trustworthy in the wild, and how to make them genuinely useful — not just impressively chatty. Today's feed captures both fronts in sharp relief.

🛡️ The Security Problem That Won't Go Away

As AI agents take on more autonomous tasks, the attack surface grows with them. @bcherny at Anthropic flagged the urgency today, announcing a new competition with Gray Swan aimed squarely at one of the field's nastiest unsolved problems:

"Over the last few years, we have made significant progress on prompt injection for Claude models. As agents do more, it is increasingly urgent that we solve it across the industry." — @bcherny

Prompt injection — where malicious inputs hijack an AI agent's instructions — is the kind of problem that sounds academic until agents are autonomously managing email, code, and business workflows. The competition framing is smart: crowdsource the adversarial creativity that internal red teams inevitably miss.

Meanwhile, @adityaag made a bullish call on interpretability startup Goodfire, arguing the field is finally maturing from philosophy into engineering:

"I strongly believe that Goodfire might be one of the most important companies to come out of @spc. They are showing that interpretability and alignment can be approached as engineering problems." — @adityaag

Dan Shipper offered a wry corrective to anyone getting too excited about interpretability breakthroughs, channeling a Good Will Hunting-style monologue:

"You're gonna believe that until next semester, when you find a neuron that lights up for the Eiffel Tower. Then you're gonna spend the summer explaining how we can align a superintelligence because we know when it's thinking about France. And next year you'll realize that knowing it recognizes the Eiffel Tower doesn't tell you what the fuck it's planning." — @danshipper

⚡ The "Intelligence Per Dollar" Revolution: Meet Jev

The most substantive conversation in today's feed centers on Jev, the model from TypeSafe that has become — in the space of a month — AI Twitter's most debated, most cloned, and least-understood launch of the year. Matt Turck sat down with TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida to unpack it.

Watch/Listen: Jev: The AI That Makes Decisions, Not Text — The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

The numbers are staggering — 40 million views on the launch video, a trillion tokens a day, a $870M Series A at a $7.5B valuation — but Almeida is conspicuously unimpressed by his own metrics. His north star is something more fundamental: a shift from intelligence per second to intelligence per dollar.

"The future is going to be intelligence per dollar primarily. And I think really getting people to play with the idea that intelligence per dollar has dropped orders of magnitude is what will make the Jevolution unstoppable independent of enterprise adoption, users, stats, whatever." — Diogo Almeida

What is Jev, exactly? The podcast describes it as "machine-native AI, built for software" — a model optimized for decisions rather than prose, closer to a composable smart if-statement than a chatbot. Critics call it "just a classifier." Almeida takes that as a compliment.

He also makes a provocative claim about his former employer: that OpenAI's RLHF training process — designed to make models pleasant and agreeable to humans — is precisely what makes them unreliable for automation.

"95% Einstein, 5% Mr. Bean. And if it doesn't tell you when it's the Mr. Bean, then how are you gonna automate anything?" — Diogo Almeida

His stealth-mode philosophy is worth noting for founders: two years of silent building, a deliberately under-promised launch, and zero marketing team. The authenticity — or at minimum the performance of authenticity — is, he argues, the only thing that's worked in AI since ChatGPT.

🌊 The Agent Tsunami: Token Consumption at Scale

Aaron Levie of Box published one of the more lucid frameworks today for understanding where agentic AI is heading — and why current token consumption figures are almost certainly a rounding error compared to what's coming.

"Moving from chatting back and forth with agents, to having agents that you spin up in the background to do useful work for you is probably on the order of 100X or 1000X more token consumption than what we're seeing today. Most work right now is essentially rate limited by our ability to process and work with information." — @levie

The vision: agent swarms deployed not just by humans, but by workflows, by triggers, and by other agents — autonomously auditing codebases, reviewing documents, QA-ing infrastructure. Levie is careful to note that much of this isn't replacing existing work but creating net new categories of work that were previously economically impossible.

Meta's release of an open-weights Muse model fit neatly into this narrative, with Levie cheering it on:

"This is going to further accelerate AI diffusion because enterprises will be able to mix and match frontier performance for orchestration and high end tasks, while being able to have low cost and tailored post-trained models for repeatable workflows." — @levie

Garry Tan echoed the open-weights enthusiasm simply: "Open weight models rising."

🎲 Signals & Asides

A few quieter notes worth tracking: @thsottiaux sent the AI world into mild frenzy with a cryptic pair of high-engagement tweets — "Either we are out of ideas or we are cooking. Time will tell" and simply "Bonjour" alongside what appears to be a new model announcement, paired with the equally cryptic "Je programme en français." A French-language coding model? Something else entirely? The 2,700+ likes suggest the community smells something significant.

Guillermo Rauch at Vercel was in full shipping mode, reacting to what appears to be a major product launch with characteristic economy of language: "What a SHIP!" and "TLDR we got Vercel zeppelin and flying cars before GTA6."

And Amanda Askell of Anthropic closed out the day with the most relatable observation in the feed: "I really like the movie 'Don't Look Up' but it's also made it hard for me to go back to having red hair." The AI alignment community contains multitudes.
html_zh:
当AI代理越来越多地接管真正的工作流程时，整个行业正在面对一个根本性问题：如何让这些系统真正可靠、可控、可信赖——从防注入攻击到机器原生智能，安全与实用正成为今日最核心的战场。

🛡️ 提示注入：Agent时代最紧迫的安全威胁

随着AI代理承担更多现实任务，安全漏洞的代价也随之倍增。Anthropic工程师 @bcherny 宣布与Gray Swan联合举办一场竞赛，专门针对Claude模型的提示注入漏洞：

"过去几年，我们在Claude模型的提示注入防御上取得了显著进展。随着Agent能做的事越来越多，在全行业层面解决这一问题变得愈发紧迫。非常期待看看你们能发现什么！"
— @bcherny

与此同时，可解释性领域也在悄然升温。@adityaag 盛赞初创公司 Goodfire，称其"可能是 @spc 孵化的最重要公司之一"，因为它正在将对齐与可解释性作为工程问题来处理——而非纯粹的学术命题。

@danshipper 则用一段犀利的改编台词，戳穿了当前可解释性研究的局限：

"你花了一个暑假解释为什么我们能对齐超级智能，就因为我们知道它在想法国。而明年你会意识到，知道它认识艾菲尔铁塔，并不能告诉你它他妈的在计划什么。"
— @danshipper

🤖 Jev：为机器而生的AI，而非为人类对话而生

本周最值得深挖的产品故事，来自 TypeSafe 及其模型 Jev。Watch/Listen: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck — Jev: The AI That Makes Decisions, Not Text

Jev 在一个月内收获了4000万次播放、每天百万用户、每天万亿tokens，并完成了 8.7 亿美元的 A 轮融资，估值 75 亿美元。但 TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida 说，这些数字都不是他真正在乎的：

"对我来说，真正的信号是当开发者开始用它做奇怪的事情，尤其是那些以前能做但嫌太贵所以没做的应用。……不管那个初始雪球有多大，它都会变得巨大。"

Jev 的核心哲学是"机器原生智能"——针对软件自动化而非人类对话进行优化。Diogo 在 OpenAI 期间曾写过一份内部文件，标题耐人寻味：

"我们本来去年就能拥有AGI。我至今仍相信这是真的。因为OpenAI对AGI的定义门槛非常低，而这些模型其实非常非常聪明——我们只是没有真正把这两件事联系起来。"

他对当前主流AI范式的批评同样直白："预训练是一场巨大的资源浪费。" Jev 选择从开源权重模型出发，用自建训练数据，专注于分类与决策任务，而非生成流畅的文本。正如他所说："Build prod, not God."（造产品，不造神。）

🌐 开源权重崛起：Meta 的一步棋，行业的千层浪

Meta 发布 Muse 开源权重模型，引发广泛反响。Box CEO @levie 给出了他认为最重要的战略意涵：

"这将进一步加速AI扩散，因为企业可以混搭前沿模型来处理编排和高端任务，同时针对可重复工作流使用低成本、定制化的微调模型。这将大幅增加整个技术栈的token消耗量。"
— @levie

Garry Tan 则简洁地总结道："开源权重模型正在崛起。"

🚀 Agent Swarm：下一个量级的token消耗

@levie 发布了一篇罕见的长文，系统阐述了从"人机对话"到"agent集群"的范式跃迁，值得全文阅读：

"从一来一回地与Agent对话，转变为在后台启动Agent为你完成真正工作，其token消耗量可能是我们今天所见的100倍甚至1000倍。……想象一下，针对任何你能想到的问题部署一个Agent群——保护代码库、对每次变更进行QA、审查每份文件寻找潜在风险……这些大多数甚至不是在替代现有工作，而是全新的增量工作。"
— @levie

他的结论是：瓶颈已不在模型能力或成本，而在于算力是否足够。这与 Jev 的"intelligence per dollar"哲学形成了有趣的呼应——当智能的边际成本趋近于零，限制想象力的将只剩下算力与信任。

💡 编辑随笔：烹饪中，还是黔驴技穷？

今天互联网上流传最广的一条推文，来自 Anthropic 研究员 @thsottiaux，只有一句话：

"要么我们已经江郎才尽，要么我们正在大厨烹饪。时间会告诉我们答案。"

2774个点赞，没有任何上下文。这大概是整个AI行业此刻最诚实的自我描述。安全竞赛、开源权重、Agent集群、机器原生智能——每一条线索都在同时向前延伸，而没有人确切知道它们最终会在哪里交汇。我们只能继续烹饪，然后等待。
